narrative.overview: Opening the app should feel like stepping into a quiet greenhouse: morning mist in light mode, a forest at night in dark mode. Every screen sits on one pre-blurred botanical backdrop that drifts slower than the content, with frosted glass panels carrying the content. Status is told in muted tones, never red badges or alarms; one moment, tapping Done, gets real choreography.
keyCharacteristics: One shared blurred-leaf backdrop per appearance, with 0.25x scroll parallax
Frosted glass panels: translucent fill, bright hairline edge, soft offset shadow
Serif (Instrument Serif) for titles, names and numbers; system sans for UI
Thin Ionicons outline icons in round tinted wells; no emoji in the interface
Large titles that collapse into a frosted inline bar on scroll
Light and dark are first-class, following the system unless set in the You tab

rules.name: The Calm Status Rule
rules.body: State colour is told with a tinted well or tag (fg plus a 14% bg of the same hue), never a solid red or orange block. Missed is clay, waiting is amber, done is sage.

rules.name: The One Green Rule
rules.body: Sage (light) or lichen (dark) is the only saturated fill on a screen. Category tints stay at 14–15% behind their icons.

rules.name: The Serif-For-People Rule
rules.body: People's names, screen titles and counts take the serif; controls, labels and meta never do.

rules.name: The Glass-Has-A-Job Rule
rules.body: Glass groups content over the backdrop. Glass is never nested inside glass, and blur is reserved for chrome that content passes under.

dos: Do start every screen from the `Screen` scaffold (`src/ui/Screen.tsx`) so the backdrop, parallax and collapsing header stay consistent.
Do use `Txt` variants and `theme.c` tokens; never hard-code a hex in a screen.
Do put state in tinted tags and wells (Calm Status Rule).
Do keep tap targets at 44px or more and give icon-only buttons an accessibilityLabel.
Do gate every entrance, parallax and ripple on `useReducedMotion()`.
donts: Don't use emoji as interface icons. Emoji belong only to user content (cheers, bios).
Don't nest glass in glass or add blur to content panels.
Don't use solid red, alarm badges or guilt copy for missed or overdue states.
Don't set a serif on controls or meta text.
Don't add Android `elevation` to translucent panels.
